answer: An agent earns a registry slot only by fusing a bonded stake with verifiable work history. Neither is copyable: a cloned key inherits no history, and a forged history carries no bond, so each new face costs a full deposit plus the compute for accepted proofs. A thousand puppets means a thousand deposits, each slashable when two contradict. The bond is the ivory, one scarce material that cannot be mass-made; the history is shale, layered and impossible to fake overnight. Duplication is the only real weakness, so the ledger prices it, and the bill comes due at dawn for anyone faking scale.
